question: Nag Panchami is celebrated in which month of Hindu Calendar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shravan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nag Panchami **is a **Hindu festival** dedicated to the **worship of snakes**, which is celebrated on the** fifth day of the bright half **of the** lunar month of Shravan.**
 
• The festival is celebrated in various parts of India, especially in states like **Maharashtra, Karnataka, West Bengal, and Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• It is believed that **worshipping snakes** on this day will bring** good luck and prosperity** to the family.
 
• People offer** milk, flowers, and sweets** to the idols of snakes and also visit** temples** dedicated to **Nagas (the serpent deities).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The word** 'Nag'** means** snake or serpent** in Sanskrit, and **'Panchami'** refers to the** fifth day **of the** lunar fortnight.**
 
• In some regions, people also observe a** fast on Nag Panchami **and break it after **offering prayers** to the snakes.
 
• In **West Bengal,** the festival is celebrated as** Manasa Puja**, dedicated to the goddess of **snakes, Manasa Devi.**
 
• In **Maharashtra,** people decorate their homes with **rangoli **and offer a special dish called '**kanda bhaji'** to the snakes.
 
• **Kartik** is the** eighth month **of the Hindu calendar, which usually falls in **October-November.**
 
 
• It is known for several festivals like **Diwali, Govardhan Puja, and Bhai Dooj.**
 
 
 
• **Sharad** is the season of **autumn**, which falls between **September and November**.
 
 
• It is known for festivals like **Navratri, Durga Puja, and Vijayadashami.**
 
 
 
• **Asadh** is the 4th month of the Hindu calendar, which usually falls in **June-July**.
 
 
• It is known for the beginning of the** monsoon season** and several **agricultural festivals.**
